question: Which place in the Garo hills of Meghalaya may receive an amount of rainfall in a day equal to 10 years of rainfall in Jaisalmer of Rajasthan ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tura** is located in the West Garo Hills district of Meghalaya.
 
• Tura receives heavy rainfall due to the southwest monsoon and its proximity to the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The region is known for its lush green hills and dense vegetation, which are sustained by significant rainfall.
 
• Tura's climate is classified as subtropical highland, contributing to its heavy rainfall patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garo Hills**

 
 
• The Garo Hills are part of the Garo-Khasi range in Meghalaya, known for their biodiversity and unique ecosystems.
 
• These hills are home to the Garo tribe, one of the major tribal communities in Meghalaya.
 
• The Garo Hills receive high rainfall due to their geographical location and elevation, influencing the local climate and vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Rainfall Patterns in India**
 
 
• India experiences varied rainfall patterns due to its diverse geography and climate zones.
 
• The southwest monsoon, occurring from June to September, is the primary source of rainfall for most parts of India.
 
• Regions like Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth, receiving extremely high annual rainfall.
 
• In contrast, areas like Jaisalmer in Rajasthan receive very low rainfall, characteristic of arid and desert climates.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Mechanism**
 
 
• The Indian monsoon is a complex meteorological phenomenon primarily influenced by the differential heating of land and ocean.
 
• During the summer, low-pressure areas develop over the Indian subcontinent, drawing moist air from the Indian Ocean.
 
• As this moist air ascends, it cools and condenses to form clouds, resulting in heavy rainfall.
 
• The Himalayas play a crucial role in trapping the moist monsoon winds, enhancing the rainfall in the northern and northeastern regions.
 
 
 
• **Cherrapunji**
 
 
• Cherrapunji, located in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, is renowned for holding records of the highest annual and monthly rainfall.
 
• It receives an average annual rainfall of around 11,777 mm.
 
• The unique topography and wind patterns contribute to its exceptional rainfall, making it a significant point of study for meteorologists.
